#### `AascVideoDecoder`

Decodes Autodesk Animator Codec (`AASC`): a run-length coding over twenty-four-bit BGR pictures, coded bottom row first, with the same shape of escapes Microsoft RLE uses at eight bits a pixel — end of row, end of frame and a delta that moves the pen without painting.

Implements `IVideoCodecDecoder<AascVideoDecoder>`, `IVideoFrameDecoder`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CodecName` | `static string CodecName { get; }` |  |
| `Accepts` | `static bool Accepts(MediaStreamInfo stream)` |  |
| `Create` | `static AascVideoDecoder Create(MediaStreamInfo stream)` |  |
| `TryDecode` | `bool TryDecode(CodedPacket packet, out RawImage frame)` | Decodes one packet, which for this codec is always exactly one whole frame. |

#### `AnimVideoDecoder`

Decodes IFF ANIM video (`ANIM`): the Amiga's own CEL animation format, whose first frame is an ordinary IFF ILBM picture and whose later frames are either that picture again or the coded difference from an earlier one — plane-major bit planar throughout, read either straight through a palette or through Hold-And-Modify, exactly the two pixel encodings this library's CDXL decoder already reads.

Implements `IVideoCodecDecoder<AnimVideoDecoder>`, `IVideoFrameDecoder`.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `CodecName` | `static string CodecName { get; }` |  |
| `Accepts` | `static bool Accepts(MediaStreamInfo stream)` |  |
| `Create` | `static AnimVideoDecoder Create(MediaStreamInfo stream)` |  |
| `TryDecode` | `bool TryDecode(CodedPacket packet, out RawImage frame)` |  |

#### `ZeroCodecVideoDecoder`

Decodes ZeroCodec: a delta coding carried entirely inside a zlib stream. Every packet is one complete, independently checksummed zlib stream that inflates to exactly one picture's worth of bytes, and a decompressed byte of zero means "the byte already held at this position is unchanged" while any other value is the literal new byte. There is no header of its own — a packet's whole payload is that zlib stream, from its first byte to its last.

Implements `IVideoCodecDecoder<ZeroCodecVideoDecoder>`, `IVideoFrameDecoder`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CodecName` | `static string CodecName { get; }` |  |
| `Accepts` | `static bool Accepts(MediaStreamInfo stream)` |  |
| `Create` | `static ZeroCodecVideoDecoder Create(MediaStreamInfo stream)` |  |
| `TryDecode` | `bool TryDecode(CodedPacket packet, out RawImage frame)` |  |

#### `ZmbvVideoDecoder`

Decodes Zip Motion Blocks Video (ZMBV), the screen-capture codec DOSBox writes: rectangular blocks copied from wherever a motion vector points in the frame before, optionally XOR'ed with a correction, the whole of it — block vectors, corrections and an intraframe's raw picture alike — riding one continuous zlib stream.

Implements `IVideoCodecDecoder<ZmbvVideoDecoder>`, `IVideoFrameDecoder`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CodecName` | `static string CodecName { get; }` |  |
| `Accepts` | `static bool Accepts(MediaStreamInfo stream)` |  |
| `Create` | `static ZmbvVideoDecoder Create(MediaStreamInfo stream)` |  |
| `TryDecode` | `bool TryDecode(CodedPacket packet, out RawImage frame)` |  |

#### `ChunkKind`

What role a chunk plays in the format. Generic categories that map onto each format's own taxonomy — for PNG: IHDR=Header, PLTE=Palette, IDAT=PixelData, IEND=Footer, eXIf/tEXt/iCCP=Metadata, the 8-byte 0x89 50 4E 47 ... preamble=Signature.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Unknown` | `0` |  |
| `Signature` | `1` | File-identifying magic bytes (always at offset 0). |
| `Header` | `2` | Top-level header with format/dimension info — usually mandatory and position-locked. |
| `PixelData` | `3` | Primary pixel/sample payload (IDAT, mdat, JPEG entropy-coded segment, ...). |
| `Palette` | `4` | Indexed-image palette table. |
| `Metadata` | `5` | Application metadata (EXIF, XMP, text comments, timestamps). |
| `ColorProfile` | `6` | Colour profile data (ICC, sRGB, gamma, chromaticity). |
| `Footer` | `7` | End-of-file marker. |
| `Padding` | `8` | Padding / filler bytes the caller may safely drop. |

#### `ChunkMobility`

What a caller may do with a chunk during rewrite. Flags compose — a movable + removable metadata chunk has `Movable | Removable`.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Fixed` | `0` | Position-locked, cannot be moved or removed (signature, IHDR, IEND). |
| `Movable` | `1` | May be relocated within the file as long as format-ordering constraints stay satisfied. |
| `Removable` | `2` | May be deleted entirely (typically ancillary metadata). |
| `Fusible` | `4` | May be merged with adjacent same-name chunks (PNG split IDATs → one IDAT, JPEG split DRI, ...). |

#### `ChunkOptimizer`

Builds a `ChunkRewritePlan` that removes byte-identical duplicate chunks, on top of the generic `IFormatChunkLayout`/`IFormatChunkPlanRewriter` substrate — this is format-agnostic: it never looks at a chunk's payload semantics, only its raw bytes, so it works for any format that exposes chunk layout, not just the metadata carriers.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SuggestDeduplicationPlan` | `static ChunkRewritePlan SuggestDeduplicationPlan(IReadOnlyList<ChunkSpan> chunks, ReadOnlySpan<byte> data, ChunkKind kind = 5)` | Finds duplicate-content chunks of a given `kind` (defaulting to `Metadata`) and returns a plan that removes every occurrence after the first. Returns an empty plan (nothing to remove) when there are no duplicates. |

#### `ChunkPlacement`

Where a chunk should end up after a rewrite. Matches the by-name policy model used by downstream tools (CompressionWorkbench MetadataPlacementProfile, web-asset post-processors) so callers don't need to reason about exact offsets.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Keep` | `0` | Keep the chunk where it is (default — no-op for rules whose chunk is already valid). |
| `BeforeData` | `1` | Move the chunk to be before the format's primary `PixelData` run. |
| `AfterData` | `2` | Move the chunk to be after the format's primary `PixelData` run (but before any mandatory footer such as PNG IEND). |
| `Remove` | `3` | Delete every instance of this chunk. The rewriter validates the chunk's `Removable` flag before honouring this. |
| `Fuse` | `4` | Merge every instance of this chunk into a single contiguous chunk in the chunk's existing position (PNG IDAT joining, JPEG split-marker fusing). Validates against `Fusible`. |

Implements `IEquatable<ChunkPlacementDirective>`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ChunkPlacementDirective` | `ChunkPlacementDirective(ChunkReference Chunk, ChunkZone TargetZone, int? OrderInZone = null)` | An explicit placement directive — "put this chunk into that zone, optionally at this order within the zone". Plan-based callers build a list of these to express a concrete desired layout. |
| `Chunk` | `ChunkReference Chunk { get; init; }` | The chunk to place (Name + Ordinal). |
| `OrderInZone` | `int? OrderInZone { get; init; }` | When multiple placements target the same zone, this controls intra-zone ordering. Lower values come first; equal values fall back to enumeration order. `null` means "preserve the chunk's existing relative order within the zone". |
| `TargetZone` | `ChunkZone TargetZone { get; init; }` | The zone the chunk should land in. Must be present in the chunk's `AllowedZones` bitmask or the rewriter will reject the directive. |

#### `ChunkZone`

The format-structural zone a chunk lives in. Zones partition the file into ordered regions; legal positions for each chunk are expressed as zone membership rather than raw byte offsets so callers don't need to do offset arithmetic.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Signature` | `0` | Magic-byte preamble (offset 0). |
| `Header` | `1` | Top-level header chunk(s) right after the signature (PNG IHDR, JPEG SOI+APP0). |
| `PreData` | `2` | Between header and the primary pixel/sample run — palettes, decoder hints, metadata that the spec requires to be read upfront. |
| `Data` | `3` | The primary pixel/sample run itself (PNG IDAT, MP4 mdat). Position-locked as a block. |
| `PostData` | `4` | After the data run but before the footer — comments, trailing metadata. |
| `Footer` | `5` | File terminator (PNG IEND, JPEG EOI). |

#### `ColorQuantizer`

Reduces a BGRA32 buffer to a palette of at most N entries using median-cut in RGBA space. Exact when the source holds no more distinct colours than the palette can address, so images that already fit a palette survive a round-trip bit-exactly.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `MapToPalette` | `static Result MapToPalette(byte[] bgra, int totalPixels, byte[] palette, byte[] alphaTable = null)` | Maps every pixel to its nearest entry in a palette the caller fixes in advance. Formats with a hardware palette (CGA, DOOM, NES, C64 …) store bare indices and re-apply that palette on read, so their indices must address it — not one a quantizer invented. |

| `Quantize` | `static Result Quantize(byte[] bgra, int totalPixels, int maxColors)` | Quantizes BGRA32 pixel data to at most `maxColors` palette entries. |

For planar YUV targets, a conventional colour interpretation is chosen when the source does not already carry one; use the overload accepting `targetColorInfo` when a container specifies an exact matrix/range/siting. |

#### `IfAttribute`

Conditionally includes a field in sequential parsing. The field is only read/written when the referenced field matches the condition. Example: `[If(nameof(Flags), Op.HasFlag, MyFlags.HasExtra)]` — only parse this field if Flags has the HasExtra bit set.Example: `[If(nameof(Version), Op.GreaterOrEqual, 2)]` — only parse this field for version 2+. When the condition is false, nullable fields get `null`; value types get `default`.

Inherits `Attribute`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IfAttribute` | `IfAttribute(string fieldName, Op op, object value)` | Conditionally includes a field in sequential parsing. The field is only read/written when the referenced field matches the condition. Example: `[If(nameof(Flags), Op.HasFlag, MyFlags.HasExtra)]` — only parse this field if Flags has the HasExtra bit set.Example: `[If(nameof(Version), Op.GreaterOrEqual, 2)]` — only parse this field for version 2+. When the condition is false, nullable fields get `null`; value types get `default`. |
| `FieldName` | `string FieldName { get; }` | Name of the field to test (must appear before this field in declaration order). |
| `Op` | `Op Op { get; }` | Comparison operator. |
| `Value` | `object Value { get; }` | Value to compare against. |

#### `ImageMetadata`

Platform-independent metadata carried alongside a `RawImage`. Every field is optional — a format that can't hold a given facet simply never populates it, and a writer that can't emit a given facet drops it explicitly (see the per-format metadata codecs) rather than inventing a substitute representation.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ImageMetadata` | `ImageMetadata()` |  |
| `DpiX` | `double? DpiX { get; init; }` | Horizontal pixel density in dots per inch, when the source format declared an absolute (not merely aspect-ratio) physical unit. `null` when the source had no density chunk, or declared a unit-less aspect ratio only — we do not fabricate a DPI value in that case. |
| `DpiY` | `double? DpiY { get; init; }` | Vertical pixel density in dots per inch. See `DpiX`. |
| `Exif` | `ExifData Exif { get; init; }` | Parsed EXIF tag data (TIFF IFD0 + optional Exif/GPS sub-IFDs). Carried by PNG's `eXIf` chunk and JPEG's EXIF-flavoured APP1 segment. |
| `IccProfileName` | `string IccProfileName { get; init; }` | The profile name from PNG's `iCCP` chunk (Latin-1, 1-79 bytes per spec). Meaningless without `IccProfile`. |
| `IccProfile` | `byte[] IccProfile { get; init; }` | Embedded ICC colour profile bytes (decompressed). Carried by PNG's `iCCP` chunk. JPEG APP2 ICC_PROFILE carriage is out of scope here, so this never survives a JPEG hop. |
| `Iptc` | `IptcData Iptc { get; init; }` | Parsed IPTC-IIM datasets. Carried by JPEG's Photoshop APP13 segment. PNG has no standard IPTC carrier, so this never survives a PNG hop. |
| `IsEmpty` | `bool IsEmpty { get; }` | True when every facet is absent — a convenience for callers deciding whether it's worth attaching this instance to a `RawImage` at all. |
| `TextEntries` | `IReadOnlyList<TextMetadataEntry> TextEntries { get; init; }` | Free-text annotations: PNG tEXt/zTXt/iTXt entries (keyword-tagged) or JPEG COM segments (keyword left empty). A codec writing to a format without a keyword concept collapses every entry into that format's plain-text carrier; see each format's metadata codec for the exact mapping it uses. |
| `XmpPacket` | `byte[] XmpPacket { get; init; }` | Raw XMP packet bytes (UTF-8 XML, as-is — XMP is deliberately not parsed, since any partial re-serialization risks silently dropping fields our model doesn't know about). Carried by PNG's `XML:com.adobe.xmp` iTXt convention and JPEG's XMP-flavoured APP1 segment. |

#### `PaletteSidecar`

Helpers for the `.pal` sidecar convention — preserves a chosen palette alongside indexed formats that don't store one on-disk (NES CHR, GameBoy tile, ZX font data, etc.).

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SidecarSuffix` | `const string SidecarSuffix` | The suffix appended to the main file path to form the sidecar path. |
| `Apply` | `static RawImage Apply(string filePath, RawImage raw)` | If a `.pal` sidecar exists next to `filePath` and `raw` is indexed, returns a new `RawImage` with the sidecar palette applied; otherwise returns `raw` unchanged. Accepts JASC-PAL text format or legacy raw-RGB binary. |
| `TryWrite` | `static bool TryWrite(string filePath, RawImage raw)` | Writes `<filePath>.pal` with the indexed image's palette in JASC-PAL text format. Best-effort — returns `false` on failure or when no sidecar is appropriate (non-indexed, no palette). |

#### `PixelAspectRatio`

Pixel aspect ratio (Numerator / Denominator) for display correction. Square pixels = (1, 1); Atari ST 4:3 stretch = (6, 5); Apple II HGR = (12, 7); NES = (8, 7); etc.

Implements `IEquatable<PixelAspectRatio>`.

How a resample decides what lies between two source pixels.

| `AllowedPaletteRanges` | `IntegerRange[] AllowedPaletteRanges { get; init; }` | Palette-size options the user can pick within this mode. `null` means full-colour (no palette). |
| `AvailablePalettes` | `FixedPalette[] AvailablePalettes { get; init; }` | Pre-defined palettes available within this mode (e.g. CGA palette variants, NES master palette). `null` means the user constructs an arbitrary palette. |

| `Dimensions` | `ValueTuple<IntegerRange, IntegerRange>[] Dimensions { get; }` | All coupled (Width, Height) options inside this mode. Always non-empty. |
| `DisplayFilter` | `DisplayFilter DisplayFilter { get; init; }` | Post-decode display filter (NTSC composite blending, PAL phase shift, etc.). Default `None`. |
| `IsIndexed` | `bool IsIndexed { get; }` | True if this mode has any palette-size constraint (i.e. needs colour reduction for full-colour source images). |
| `MaxColourCount` | `int MaxColourCount { get; }` | Maximum colour count this mode can encode. Returns `int.MaxValue` for full-colour modes. |
| `Name` | `string Name { get; }` | Human-readable name shown in the mode picker (e.g. "Low resolution", "Mode 13h", "Tilesheet (2bpp)"). |
| `PixelAspectRatio` | `PixelAspectRatio? PixelAspectRatio { get; init; }` | Pixel aspect ratio for display. `null` = square (1:1). Drives the viewer's X-axis scale. |
| `MatchesDimensions` | `bool MatchesDimensions(int width, int height)` | True if any of this mode's `Dimensions` entries accepts the given (width, height). |

#### `WireType`

Wire representation types for fields where the on-disk encoding differs from the C# type.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Native` | `0` | Default: native binary representation matching the C# type. |
| `BCD` | `1` | Binary-Coded Decimal. Each nibble encodes one decimal digit (0-9). 4 bytes = 8 digits. |
| `ZigZag` | `2` | ZigZag encoding (protobuf-style): maps signed integers to unsigned ((n << 1) ^ (n >> 31)). |
| `GrayCode` | `3` | Gray code: reflected binary code where adjacent values differ by one bit. |
| `VLQ` | `4` | Variable-length quantity (VLQ): 7 bits per byte, MSB continuation bit. Used in MIDI, ASN.1. |
| `ULEB128` | `5` | LEB128 unsigned: variable-length little-endian base-128. Used in DWARF, WebAssembly. |
| `SLEB128` | `6` | LEB128 signed: variable-length signed little-endian base-128. |
| `Q15_16` | `7` | Q15.16 signed fixed-point: 16-bit integer part + 16-bit fractional part → float/double property. |
| `Q1_15` | `8` | Q1.15 signed fixed-point: 1-bit sign + 15-bit fraction → float/double property. |
| `Q8_8` | `9` | Q8.8 unsigned fixed-point: 8-bit integer + 8-bit fraction → float/double property. |
| `UQ16_16` | `10` | Q16.16 unsigned fixed-point: 16-bit integer + 16-bit fraction → float/double property. |
| `Float16` | `11` | IEEE 754 half-precision (16-bit, 1+5+10). Maps to System.Half or float. |
| `M4E3` | `12` | Minifloat M4E3 (8-bit, 4-bit mantissa + 3-bit exponent + sign). Used in some GPU formats. |
| `M3E5` | `13` | Minifloat M3E5 (8-bit, 3-bit mantissa + 5-bit exponent + sign). Used in some HDR formats. |
| `BFloat16` | `14` | Brain floating-point bfloat16 (16-bit, 1+8+7). Truncated float32 used in ML. |
| `UInt24` | `15` | Unsigned 24-bit integer (3 bytes). Maps to int/uint property. |
| `Int24` | `16` | Signed 24-bit integer (3 bytes, two's complement). Maps to int property. |
| `UInt48` | `17` | Unsigned 48-bit integer (6 bytes). Maps to long/ulong property. |
| `Int96` | `18` | 96-bit integer (12 bytes). Maps to a custom Int96 type or decimal. |
| `UInt128` | `19` | Unsigned 128-bit integer (16 bytes). Maps to System.UInt128 (.NET 7+). |
| `Int128` | `20` | Signed 128-bit integer (16 bytes). Maps to System.Int128 (.NET 7+). |
| `OctalString` | `21` | Octal ASCII string: null-terminated octal digits → integer. Used in TAR headers. |
| `DecimalString` | `22` | Decimal ASCII string: fixed-width decimal digits → integer. Used in Scitex CT. |
| `HexString` | `23` | Hex ASCII string: fixed-width hex digits → integer. |

#### `VmdContainer`

A Sierra VMD file (`.vmd`) — "Video and Music Data", the format behind Phantasmagoria, Gabriel Knight 2 and Sierra's other CD-ROM adventures — taken apart into its header fields and the packets its table of contents describes, and nothing else.

Implements `IVideoContainerReader<VmdContainer>`, `IVideoFormatMetadata<VmdContainer>`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VmdContainer` | `VmdContainer()` |  |
| `AudioFrameLength` | `int AudioFrameLength { get; init; }` | The audio frame length the header states, in samples — negative in the header for sixteen-bit sound, unsigned here since nothing in this container reads sound. |
| `AudioSampleRate` | `int AudioSampleRate { get; init; }` | The audio sample rate the header states, in hertz, or zero for a file with none. |
| `BlockOffsets` | `IReadOnlyList<int> BlockOffsets { get; init; }` | Each block's own absolute file offset, in the order the block offset table states them. Not needed to walk the frame data sequentially — see `VmdReader`'s remarks — but needed for the one thing this table exists for: naming which block a video frame belongs to, which is the presentation timestamp `ReadPackets` reports for it. A block may hold more than one audio frame and no video frame at all — measured directly against a real file, where a run of blocks carrying only extra sound leaves the timestamps of the video frames around them further apart than one block — so a plain running count of video frames does not reproduce it and the block table is what does. |
| `CodecVersion` | `int CodecVersion { get; init; }` | The video codec version the header states — `1` for the eight-bit palettised form every sample this reader was measured against carries. Left for the codec to read and to refuse by name, the same way a container never itself refuses a codec it has not decoded. |

| `HasAudio` | `bool HasAudio { get; init; }` | Whether the file carries sound: the header's own flag, corroborated by at least one audio-type record actually present in the table of contents. |
| `HeaderPayload` | `ReadOnlyMemory<byte> HeaderPayload { get; init; }` | The 816-byte header verbatim, carried through as the video stream's private data so the codec can read the codec version and the initial palette this container does not interpret. |
| `Height` | `int Height { get; init; }` | Picture height in pixels. |
| `MultimediaDataOffset` | `uint MultimediaDataOffset { get; init; }` | Where the coded frame data begins — always 816, immediately after the fixed-size header, in every sample this reader was measured against. |

Everything registered for a single container format. Produced by the source-generated `VideoFormatRegistration.RegisterAll()` at startup; every operation is a typed delegate over static interface dispatch, so nothing here is reached by reflection.
